problem_type: React Flow mid-pan wheel takeover double translation
symptom: After holding the primary mouse button to pan, zooming with the wheel, and moving the pointer another 10 pixels, the canvas translated 20 pixels instead of continuing from the zoomed viewport by exactly 10 pixels.
direct_cause: The Nomi host synchronously added the post-wheel pointer delta while React Flow's native pan listener remained active and added the same delta again later in the same event.
class_root: The post-wheel takeover had two concurrent viewport writers and no reconciliation boundary that assigned a single final viewport to each pointer-move frame.
affected_population: Canvas users who zoom with the wheel while a primary-button pan is still held
Users on platforms where React Flow continues its native pan listener after wheel zoom
Users on platforms where the native listener instead keeps a stale drag baseline and can jump back
entry_points: Blank-canvas primary-button pan followed by bare-wheel zoom
Blank-canvas primary-button pan followed by modified-wheel or trackpad zoom
One or more pointer moves before the next animation frame after a mid-pan zoom
internal_only_reason: The required behavior is Nomi's existing 10-pixel pan/zoom-mix interaction contract. The failure comes from the ordering of Nomi's React capture handler and the installed React Flow listener in the real Electron build; external documentation cannot decide Nomi's final viewport ownership or regression threshold.
invariants: Every post-wheel pointer delta contributes exactly once to the final viewport.
Nomi computes one target viewport from the last reconciled target and queues at most one animation-frame write.
The queued write runs after native event handling and converges both native-continuation and stale-baseline outcomes to the same target.
Pointer end flushes any queued target before persisting the category viewport.
The real Electron pan-zoom-mix journey proves a 10-pixel pointer move produces a 10-pixel viewport delta without changing the zoom.
migration: No project or viewport schema migration is required. Pending takeover targets exist only for the active pointer gesture and are flushed or cancelled before teardown.
residual_risks: A browser that applies an additional native pan after requestAnimationFrame would require disabling the native listener explicitly; the supported Electron build applies native movement during the pointer event and is covered by the real journey.
Touch pinch gestures do not enter the primary-mouse takeover path and retain React Flow ownership.
